neet_phy_u16_t09_1.working: Frequency is set by the source and stays the same at a boundary. Speed and wavelength change, and direction changes for oblique incidence.

neet_phy_u16_t09_3.working: sin i / sin r = v1/v2 = sqrt3, so sin r = (sqrt3/2)/sqrt3 = 1/2, giving r = 30 degrees.

neet_phy_u16_t09_4.working: A: sin i/sin r = v1/v2 (III). B: lambda2 = lambda1 n1/n2 (II). C: frequency is unchanged (I). D: corpuscular theory predicts a greater speed in the denser medium (IV). This matches A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

neet_phy_u16_t09_5.working: A is true: light bends toward the normal when it slows. B is true: equal wavelet distances in equal times give i = r. C is false: sin i/sin r = n2/n1, not n1/n2. D is false: reflection changes neither wavelength nor frequency. E is true: Huygens' construction explains TIR and the critical angle. So A, B and E only.
